sceneSpec.setting: Putting green during a match play round
sceneSpec.players: Two players: Alison preparing for a putt, Jezz positioned directly behind Alison's line of play, crouching.
sceneSpec.ballPosition: On the putting green, close to the hole
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: Just as Alison is about to putt, with Jezz directly behind her line.
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Demonstrates that standing behind an opponent's line is not a breach of the Rules in match play, though it may be poor etiquette.
mustShow: A putting green with a visible hole
Alison addressing her ball and preparing to putt
Jezz clearly behind Alison, crouching on her line of play
Both players in appropriate golf attire

questions.title: Standing Behind Where Someone Aims in a Match (Match Play)
questions.question: In match play, Jezz kneels down right behind the line where Alison is putting. What happens?
questions.explanation: It’s not polite, but the rules don’t give a penalty if someone stands behind where you aim in match play.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A type of golf game where you try to win more holes than your opponent.
The direction you want your ball to go on the green.

questions.teachingTip: You can talk about being respectful to others even though the rules don’t give a penalty for standing behind someone in match play.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think there is always a penalty for standing behind someone’s line.
Children may mix up rules for stroke play and match play.

questions.title: Standing Behind an Opponent's Line in Match Play
questions.question: In match play, Jezz crouches directly behind Alison's line of play as she takes her putt. What is the ruling?
questions.explanation: The Rules do not prohibit a player or opponent from standing directly behind another player's line of play. It may be considered poor etiquette, but there is no Rules penalty.
